title: Componentwise covers induce epimorphisms of realized formal families
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category, $J$ a precoverage whose generated Grothendieck topology is subcanonical [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $T\in\mathcal C$. Let $f=(\alpha,(f_i)):X\to Y$ be a morphism of formal families in $\mathcal C/T$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct]. Suppose that for each target index $j$, the arrows $X_i\to Y_j$ for $\alpha(i)=j$ form a $J$-covering family. Then the morphism $R_T(f)$ between the coproducts of representable sheaves in the slice over $h_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct-sheaf-finite-limits] is an epimorphism. No pullback or precoverage stability hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 01G3, definition-covering, and Tag 0DB1, the implication from a formal matching cover to an epimorphism after sheafification; use the equivalent cancellation argument by sheaf separatedness.

proof.text: Given two maps g,h from R_T(Y) to a sheaf over h_T whose composites with R_T(f) agree, use the target coproduct universal property to test g=h on each representable summand h_{Y_j}.

By sheaf Yoneda, those restricted maps correspond to two sections of the target sheaf over Y_j. The componentwise covering hypothesis and separatedness of that sheaf show that they agree if their restrictions along all X_i to Y_j agree. This includes empty covering families.

Each required restriction equality is obtained by precomposing the assumed equality with the corresponding source coproduct inclusion. Substitute alpha(i)=j and use the defining equation for the map of coproducts. Faithfulness of the forgetful functor from the slice gives equality in the slice. Thus cancellation holds, proving R_T(f) epi.
